review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the neighbouring FDeriv/Add.lean simp attributes and the `deriv_id` lemmas in Deriv/Basic.lean. I did not run Lean, so these are interface-consistency findings and I did not observe any simp behaviour. The `deriv`/`deriv_fun` add, sub and sum lemmas look sensible. Some neg and id specializations overlap with other simp lemmas, but they appear to give the same normal form, so I did not report them. I am uncertain whether leaving `hasDerivAtFilter_const_add_iff` out of the simp set was deliberate. Its add_const sibling and its HasStrictDerivAt, HasDerivWithinAt and HasDerivAt specializations are all `@[simp]`.

findings.excerpt:
theorem hasDerivAtFilter_const_add_iff (c : F) :
    HasDerivAtFilter (c + f ·) f' L ↔ HasDerivAtFilter f f' L :=
findings.problem: This is the only lemma in its add/const family without `@[simp]`. Its mirror `hasDerivAtFilter_add_const_iff` is simp, and so are all three specializations of it (`hasStrictDerivAt_const_add_iff`, `hasDerivWithinAt_const_add_iff`, `hasDerivAt_const_add_iff`). The underlying `hasFDerivAtFilter_const_add_iff` is simp too. As a result `HasDerivAtFilter (c + f ·) f' L` is not reduced to `HasDerivAtFilter f f' L` by simp, although `HasDerivAt`, `HasDerivWithinAt` and `HasStrictDerivAt` are.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `hasDerivAtFilter_const_add_iff`, as for `hasDerivAtFilter_add_const_iff`. The rewrite goes in the canonical direction, from the shifted function to `f`. It has no hypotheses, and the LHS pattern is no more general than the already-simp specializations.
findings.benefit: The simp normal form is the same for all four predicates, and the add_const and const_add cases behave alike. Users stating results about `HasDerivAtFilter` with a constant added on the left no longer need to rewrite by hand.

findings.excerpt:
theorem derivWithin_add_const (c : F) :
    derivWithin (fun y ↦ f y + c) s x = derivWithin f s x := by
findings.problem: The `derivWithin` constant-shift lemmas are inconsistent. For `c + f ·` and `f · - c` there is a simp lemma in function form (`derivWithin_const_add_fun`, `derivWithin_sub_const_fun`). For `f · + c` there is no simp lemma at all. `derivWithin_add_const` is not simp, and the file has no `derivWithin_add_const_fun`. Unlike `deriv_add_const'`, nothing rewrites `derivWithin (fun y ↦ f y + c)` when it appears unapplied, and the applied form is not simplified either. The underlying `fderivWithin_add_const` is `@[simp]`, so simp normalizes `fderivWithin` but not `derivWithin`. `derivWithin_const_sub` likewise has no function-form simp lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Add a function-form lemma `derivWithin_add_const_fun (c : F) : derivWithin (f · + c) s = derivWithin f s`, proved by `ext; apply derivWithin_add_const`, and mark it `@[simp]`. This mirrors `derivWithin_sub_const_fun`. (As in `derivWithin_const_add_fun`, the function-form statement could leave `s` implicit and drop it from the statement.) Alternatively mark `derivWithin_add_const` itself `@[simp]`. Consider the same for `derivWithin_const_sub`.
findings.benefit: `derivWithin` of `f · + c` simplifies the same way as `deriv`, `f · - c` and `c + f ·`, applied or not. Users no longer need a manual `derivWithin_add_const` rewrite, and the simp normal form is uniform across the sign/side variants.
